No, Pluto is not classified as a planet under the current scientific definition. [d1] NASA's official Solar System Exploration page states that "Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt," not a full planet. [d4] According to Britannica, in 2006 the International Astronomical Union (IAU) demoted Pluto from its position as the ninth planet to a dwarf planet because "it is not big enough to exert its orbital dominance and clear the neighborhood surrounding its orbit." [d2] Wikipedia further explains that the IAU's 2006 resolution established three criteria for planethood, and "Pluto fails to meet the third condition," as its mass is substantially less than the combined mass of other objects in its orbit. [d3] Science News Explores confirms that Pluto "didn't pass the third test" of clearing its orbital neighborhood, and [d5] BBC News notes that in 2006 Pluto "was relegated to the status of dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union (IAU)."
